evidence: Deepseek checks "c in adj[a]" while iterating neighbors of a and b; GLM states "For a triple (a, b, c) ... c in adj[b]"; the other solutions build adjacency sets/bitsets and search the same structure.
affordance_in_statement: A selection of three modules is considered fatal if and only if every pair of modules within that selection interferes with each other according to the logs.
removal_suggestion: None without changing the task: detecting a three-vertex clique is the required computation, and the lexicographic tie-break is immutable.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Enumerates a and b in increasing order and returns the first common neighbor c, thereby obtaining the lexicographically smallest triangle.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: If multiple fatal selections exist, output the one with the smallest value for a; if there is a tie, choose the one with the smallest value for b; and if still tied, the smallest value for c.

common_affordance: The task is intrinsically the detection of a three-vertex clique (a triangle) in an undirected graph, equivalently a common-neighbor check.
recommended_edit: No wording edit can defeat all survivors while preserving the task; the shared affordance is the core specification rather than incidental wording.
